questions.stem: What can a reviewer do with a role that was assigned by automated criteria?
choices: Revoke it directly from the certification
Acknowledge it only, because the role model controls the assignment
Remove the lifecycle state that granted it from the same row
Convert it into a standalone entitlement and then revoke that
questions.explanation: Automated role assignments can only be acknowledged. The role model, not the certification decision, controls whether the identity keeps the role.

questions.stem: Which access profiles show up as their own rows in a certification?
choices: Profiles granted through a role or a lifecycle state
Profiles the user requested, or that were detected from entitlements they already hold
Every access profile on the source, whether or not the user has it
Only profiles that were granted in the last 90 days
questions.explanation: Profiles granted by a role are managed through that role. Profiles on a lifecycle state do not appear in the certification at all. Requested or detected profiles can be certified.

questions.stem: Who receives a certification when the identity has no manager?
choices: The source owner
The campaign owner
The org admin
The identity themselves
questions.explanation: The certification goes to the identity's manager. If there is no manager, it is sent to the owner of the campaign.

questions.stem: What happens to a revoke decision that was never signed off when the campaign completes?
choices: It is provisioned anyway
It is treated as if no decision was made
It becomes a manual task for the source owner immediately
It is held until the next campaign
questions.explanation: Revokes that are not signed off are not applied. At campaign completion, unsigned certifications are treated as though no decisions were made. The campaign configuration then decides whether those items are auto-approved.

questions.stem: How many identity profiles can one identity belong to?
choices: One, and the highest-priority authoritative source wins if the person exists in several
One per authoritative source they appear in
As many as have a matching email address
Two: the authoritative profile and a secondary profile
questions.explanation: Each identity is associated with only one identity profile. If the person exists in multiple authoritative sources, priority order decides which profile they join.

questions.stem: Which identity attributes are required on every identity profile?
choices: User Name, Work Email, and Last Name, and none of them can be null
Department, Manager, and Location
User Name only
Work Email and Manager, and the email must pass format validation
questions.explanation: User Name (uid), Work Email (email), and Last Name (lastname) must be mapped and cannot be null. User Name must also be unique across every identity profile. Work Email is not validated as an email address.

questions.stem: Which characters cannot be used in the source attribute mapped to a username?
choices: Spaces and hyphens
The characters * ( ) & ! .
Only characters outside ASCII
Digits
questions.explanation: If the username or another sign-in attribute includes * ( ) & ! or a period, the identity may be unable to sign in.

questions.stem: What is the maximum size of a form, including the user's responses?
choices: 40 kilobytes
400 kilobytes
4 megabytes
There is no size limit
questions.explanation: If the form, including responses, exceeds 400 kilobytes, it cannot be saved or submitted.

questions.stem: What is submitted when a user leaves a form field blank?
choices: The placeholder text
The default value, if one was set; placeholder text is never submitted
Both the placeholder and the default
An empty string, and a default is ignored
questions.explanation: Placeholder text is guidance only. A default value is submitted when the user does not enter a response, and it overrides the placeholder.

questions.stem: What happens to an access request that is still not fully approved after 90 days?
choices: It is automatically denied and expired, unless timeoutConfig says otherwise
It stays open until an admin closes it
It is auto-approved
It is returned to the requester to start over
questions.explanation: The default is to deny and expire the request after 90 days. timeoutConfig on the approvals configuration can shorten that window and can instead auto-approve expired requests.

questions.stem: Who can open Identity Graph, and what does data segmentation do there?
choices: Any user, and segmentation hides identities outside their segment
An Org Admin, Identity Graph Admin, or Identity Graph Read Only user, and the dashboard widget is not segmented
Only the campaign owner, and segmentation applies to every object
Source Sub-Admins, and they see only their source
questions.explanation: Access requires one of those three user levels. Data segmentation does not apply to the Identity Graph dashboard widget, so anyone who can open it sees every access object and identity in the tenant.

questions.stem: In an adaptive approval, how does Quorum differ from Multi-Step?
choices: Quorum requires every reviewer to approve; Multi-Step uses a percentage
Multi-Step fails if any reviewer denies; Quorum fails only once the configured approval percentage can no longer be reached
They are the same policy with two names
Quorum is a single reviewer, and Multi-Step is a sequence
questions.explanation: Multi-Step needs every reviewer, and one denial fails the item. Quorum uses a percentage you set, and a single rejection does not fail the request until that percentage is impossible. Serial is the ordered variant.

questions.stem: What are the five components of the Shared Signals Framework?
choices: Subject, Event, Transmitter, Receiver, and Stream
Sender, Token, Webhook, Policy, and Action
Identity, Role, Entitlement, Source, and Campaign
Detector, Correlator, Approver, Certifier, and Reporter
questions.explanation: A subject is who the event is about. A transmitter broadcasts events, a receiver acts on them, and a stream is how events flow between the two. Workflows define what SailPoint does when a supported event arrives.

questions.stem: Who can discover and classify machine accounts?
choices: Any account owner
An Org Admin, a Source Admin, or a Source Sub-Admin who belongs to that source's governance group
Only the certification reviewer
The primary owner of an application identity
questions.explanation: Those three admin roles can discover, classify, and manage machine accounts. Account owners may review application identities and their access in a certification, which is a narrower right.

questions.stem: What is an application identity?
choices: A human identity that owns a source
A machine identity that groups the machine accounts for one program or service
A subtype used only for bots
The entitlement that grants Domain Admin
questions.explanation: Related machine accounts are correlated to the application identity so they can be reviewed as one program or service instead of as disconnected accounts.

questions.stem: How many additional owners can an application identity have, and who inherits it?
choices: Up to 10. If the primary owner becomes inactive, the first Active additional owner inherits it
One additional owner, who must be the primary owner's manager
Unlimited owners, and they all stay owners after they become inactive
None. Ownership cannot be shared
questions.explanation: You can name up to 10 additional owners. Inactive identities are removed from that list. If none remain, ownership passes to the primary owner's manager, and if there is no manager the application has no primary owner until one is added.

questions.stem: How many user entitlements can grant access to one application identity?
choices: 10, and they can come from more than one source
There is no maximum
questions.explanation: The create flow allows a maximum of 10 user entitlements from multiple sources. They are visible afterward on the application identity's Details tab.

questions.stem: What belongs in the Native Identity field when you create an application identity?
choices: The primary owner's email
A unique value that describes the program or service, matching the stored attribute when you have one
The source name
The certification campaign id
questions.explanation: The name must be unique so people can tell application identities apart. Native Identity is the value used to correlate machine accounts when that value is already stored on the accounts.

questions.stem: Where do you create an application identity?
choices: Admin > Identity Management > Identities, then Applications under Machine Identities
Admin > Global > System Settings
The certification campaign wizard
The source's account schema
questions.explanation: Create Application is on the Applications list in the Machine Identities section. You then set the name, native identity, primary owner, and optional additional owners.

questions.stem: When should you create application identities if you do not store application data?
choices: Before any source is configured
After machine accounts have been classified on a source
Only during the first aggregation, and never again
After the certification campaign is signed off
questions.explanation: If application data lives in a database you can create the identities earlier. Without that data, classification comes first, and the application identity is what the classified accounts correlate to.

questions.stem: What do you do when several uncorrelated application identities represent the same service?
choices: Certify each of them separately forever
Create one application identity and correlate the related machine accounts to it
Delete the machine accounts
Merge them by giving them the same primary owner email
questions.explanation: One application identity represents the program. Correlating the accounts to it is what lets SailPoint review that service as a single identity.

questions.stem: Which implementation step classifies future machine accounts, not only the ones already aggregated?
choices: Creating machine account subtypes and classification criteria
Inviting the account owners to the tenant
Running a manager certification
Enabling Password Management
questions.explanation: Subtypes describe type and function. Criteria decide which source accounts are classified as machine accounts, including accounts aggregated later. Mappings then copy attributes onto the machine account.

questions.stem: What can an account owner do with machine identities?
choices: Change the classification policy
Review application identities and their access during a certification
Create sources
Delete the identity profile
questions.explanation: Classification and management stay with Org Admin, Source Admin, or a Source Sub-Admin in the governance group. Account owners are limited to certification review.

questions.stem: What is the last step of a machine-identity implementation in the product docs?
choices: A machine account certification campaign
Deleting uncorrelated accounts automatically
Replacing the authoritative source
Disabling human certifications
questions.explanation: After classification, mappings, and review, you create a certification so owners can verify the machine accounts and the access they hold. Uncorrelated accounts are certified too if you have not grouped them yet.

questions.stem: Who becomes the owner if the primary owner is deleted and no additional owner was named?
choices: The primary owner's manager, or nobody if that manager does not exist
The org admin automatically
The source owner
The oldest machine account on the source
questions.explanation: Succession tries additional owners first, then the manager. With neither, the application has no primary owner until someone adds one.

questions.stem: What does Machine Identity Security let you request, besides reviewing accounts?
choices: Creation or deletion of a machine account
A new identity profile
A Harbor Pilot prompt
An emergency access id in SAP
questions.explanation: The overview lists discovery, classification, correlation to an application identity, certification, a cross-source view, and requests to create or delete a machine account.

questions.stem: What does the product documentation call an AI agent?
choices: A human identity with an API token
A machine identity that uses a large language model to perform tasks for a user or another system
A browser extension
A certification campaign type
questions.explanation: Agent Identity Security treats the agent as a machine identity. Onboarding it into Human Fabric is what makes it discoverable and governable with other identities.

questions.stem: Which outcome is specifically about the humans who use an agent?
choices: Preventing those identities from gaining excessive permissions through the agent
Replacing their identity profile
Disabling their Human Fabric login
Moving them to a lifecycle state of inactive
questions.explanation: The documented outcomes are discovery, governing agents next to human and application identities, assigning multiple owners, and stopping humans from inheriting excessive access through an agent.

questions.stem: How can an AI agent get into Human Fabric if it is not on a supported source dataset?
choices: It cannot. Aggregation is the only path
An admin can create the agent on the AI Agents list
It is created automatically from a certification
Harbor Pilot creates it when someone mentions the agent in a prompt
questions.explanation: You aggregate agents through dataset aggregations, and you can also create one in the tenant when a source account represents an agent. Creation starts at Admin > Identity Management > Identities > AI Agents.

questions.stem: What do generic sources need before their agents aggregate correctly?
choices: A virtual appliance only
Datasets and resources so the attributes map to the non-human identity
A password policy
An identity profile set as authoritative
questions.explanation: Supported sources have preconfigured datasets. Generic sources need datasets and resources you create, including the schema, or the aggregated attributes will not represent the agent.

questions.stem: After aggregation, what do you configure so an agent is not left without an owner?
choices: Owners and an automated succession plan
A Shared Signals receiver
A form with a 400 kilobyte limit
An Express Setup connector
questions.explanation: The implementation steps assign owners and a succession plan, then tell you to review attributes, the humans who can reach the agent, and the tools the agent's machine accounts can reach.

questions.stem: Which report does the documentation tell you to run for humans who can reach an agent?
choices: Identities Overpermissioned by Agents
Account Activity
Lifecycle State Refresh
Security Audit Log
questions.explanation: You can list identities who hold the user entitlement for the agent, and you can run that report. Certification campaigns then let a reviewer decide whether the access should remain.

questions.stem: How many additional owners can an AI agent have?
choices: Up to 10 human identities
Only governance groups, not people
questions.explanation: Same ceiling as an application identity. If the primary owner becomes inactive, the first Active additional owner takes over. Inactive identities are removed from the additional-owners list.

questions.stem: Who owns the agent if the primary owner is deleted and no additional owner was set?
choices: The primary owner's manager, or no one if there is no manager
The org admin
The source's oldest account
The agent owns itself
questions.explanation: Succession is explicit in the create flow. Without an additional owner or a manager, the agent has no primary owner until one is added manually.

questions.stem: How many user entitlements can grant a person access to one AI agent?
choices: A maximum of 10, from more than one source
One entitlement on the authoritative source
There is no limit
Only entitlements created by a workflow
questions.explanation: You select those entitlements when you create the agent. Afterward they are listed on the agent's Details tab.

questions.stem: What should you review on the machine accounts correlated to an agent?
choices: The access entitlements those accounts hold, which are the agent's tools
The agent's Human Fabric password
The identity profile priority
The form's placeholder text
questions.explanation: The agent's reach is the entitlements on its correlated machine accounts. The docs tell you to view those entitlements and to certify them.

questions.stem: Why review accounts the classification policy may have missed?
choices: A policy can fail to mark a machine account that should be correlated to an agent
Missed accounts are deleted after 24 hours
Only missed accounts can be certified
The policy disables accounts it does not recognize
questions.explanation: The steps say to review possible machine accounts the classification policy missed, then map or update their attributes before you correlate them.

questions.stem: What makes the Native Identity of an agent different from its name?
choices: Native Identity is a unique value describing the agent, used to tell it apart in correlation; the name is the label people see
They must be identical
Native Identity is the primary owner's uid
The name is written to the source and Native Identity is only a comment
questions.explanation: Both must be unique. The name helps people distinguish agents. Native Identity describes the agent itself.

questions.stem: Can machine accounts that an agent uses stay unclassified?
choices: No. The documented path classifies them on the source and then correlates them to the agent
Yes. Correlation does not require a subtype
Only if they are human accounts
Only when Agent Identity Security is not licensed
questions.explanation: The steps create a subtype, set a classification policy, review misses, map attributes, and then correlate those accounts to the agent.

questions.stem: What is Agentic Fabric, in the product documentation?
choices: A replacement for Human Fabric
An agent-governance capability inside Human Fabric for AI agents and other non-human identities
A File Access Manager module
A connector for SAP only
questions.explanation: It discovers agents and non-human identities across enterprise, endpoint, and browser surfaces, ties them to human owners, and classifies usage against policy. It includes onboarding, a registry, Identity Graph, and audit reporting.

questions.stem: What kind of cloud access does onboarding ask you to provide?
choices: Write access so Agentic Fabric can disable agents in AWS
Read-only access so it can discover agents on AWS, Azure, and other AI platforms
The root credentials for every account
No cloud connection. The browser extension is sufficient
questions.explanation: Onboarding connects the systems used for discovery and for correlating agents to the people who own them. Cloud platform access is read-only.

questions.stem: What does the non-human identity registry let an admin do after activation?
choices: Evaluate non-human identities by risk, manage ownership, and organize agents into business apps
Reset human passwords
Replace identity profiles
Approve access requests for employees
questions.explanation: The registry is the single view of enterprise, endpoint, and browser agents. Ownership can be individual identities or governance groups.

questions.stem: Which agent types does the registry distinguish?
choices: Enterprise, browser, and endpoint, plus Unknown when a new agent is not yet classified
Human, contractor, and guest
Joiner, mover, and leaver
Only agents that have a primary owner
questions.explanation: Unknown is used when Agentic Fabric sees activity it has not classified yet, including a newer agent. Business app, status, and owners are the other columns the registry shows.

questions.stem: Which quick filters does the Agent Registry provide?
choices: Discovered in the last 30 days, unsanctioned, and missing an owner
Failed certifications and expired passwords
Identities with no email address
Sources that have not aggregated today
questions.explanation: Those filters are on the Agent Registry page. More filters can be added, and Clear All Filters removes them.

questions.stem: What can you change from an agent's details page?
choices: Its active or inactive status, and you can inspect attributes, user entitlements, and change history
The tenant's identity profile priority
The SAP audit log format
Whether Harbor Pilot can edit workflows
questions.explanation: Activate and deactivate are documented actions. The Details tab shows attributes and the user entitlements that grant people access to the agent.

questions.stem: What does a warning on a business app mean in the registry?
choices: The app is unsanctioned
The app failed to aggregate human accounts
The app is the authoritative source
The app has no virtual appliance
questions.explanation: The business app column can warn when the organization has not sanctioned that app. The agent is still listed so you can see the association.

questions.stem: Does onboarding have to be finished in one sitting?
choices: No. You can skip steps and return to them later
Yes. Activation fails if any step is skipped
Only the identity provider step can be skipped
Steps lock after the first sign-on
questions.explanation: The guided onboarding lets you work in whatever order fits. Unfinished steps stay available after you leave.

questions.stem: What is embedded in Agentic Fabric besides the registry?
choices: Identity Graph, endpoint and browser discovery, ownership and lifecycle controls, and audit-ready reporting
Password interception only
SAP emergency access
A replacement certification engine
questions.explanation: The overview lists those capabilities together. Discovery connects agents to human owners and classifies usage against policy.

questions.stem: Where do you open the list of agents?
choices: Agentic Fabric, then Agents under Non-Human Identities
Admin > Global > Forms
The certification campaign owner page
Identity profiles
questions.explanation: The Agent Registry is in the Non-Human Identities section. Accounts for machine, service, and bot accounts are a separate page in that same section.

questions.stem: What label does discovery add when it thinks an account is an agent?
choices: Discovered as Agent
Unsanctioned human
Lifecycle state inactive
Manual remediation
questions.explanation: Machine Account Discovery reviews updated accounts daily. Discovered as Machine and Discovered as Agent are the two labels, and each one explains why the account was flagged.

questions.stem: What should you do with an account that was discovered as a machine identity?
choices: Correlate it to a machine identity after you confirm it is non-human
Delete it immediately
Invite it as a human user
Put it on an identity profile
questions.explanation: The Discovered Accounts tile shows why the account was recommended. If it is non-human, you select it and correlate it to a machine identity. Several accounts can be correlated together.

questions.stem: What powers agent discovery and monitoring besides cloud sources and the identity provider?
choices: A connection to your EDR or SIEM
A nightly CSV upload only
The password reset flow
IdentityIQ task servers
questions.explanation: Onboarding connects an identity provider, cloud platforms as read-only sources, and your EDR or SIEM. Once connected, Agentic Fabric uses those data sources for discovery and monitoring.

questions.stem: What does SailPoint Entro continuously discover and protect?
choices: Human passwords in Active Directory only
Secrets such as credentials, API keys, and tokens, including other non-human identities
Certification decisions
Identity profile mappings
questions.explanation: Entro's stated scope is credentials, API keys, tokens, and other non-human identities, wherever they sit in the environment.

questions.stem: Where does the documentation say those secrets are found?
choices: Only inside a vault
Source code, configuration files, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party integrations
Only in email
Only on virtual appliances
questions.explanation: The visibility gap Entro is written to close is between cloud providers, developer tools, and internal systems, not only the secrets that already reached a vault.

questions.stem: What is Entro trying to stop before it happens?
choices: Secret leakage, unauthorized access, and privilege escalation
Failed human certifications
Identity profile priority conflicts
Form submissions over 400 kilobytes
questions.explanation: That is the stated purpose: secure the development ecosystem by finding the exposure early, rather than after a credential has been misused.

questions.stem: How is a secret's risk level decided?
choices: It is static and based only on the file name
Dynamically, from privilege, rotation, and exposure
By the number of lines in the repository
Only by whether the secret is in GitHub
questions.explanation: Context-aware analysis prioritizes exposed or at-risk secrets. Privilege, whether it rotates, and where it is exposed all feed the risk level.

questions.stem: Which systems does the about page list as natively supported?
choices: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jenkins, AWS, Azure, GCP, Slack, and Atlassian Cloud
SAP ECC and IdentityIQ only
Active Directory and Workday only
ServiceNow and nothing else
questions.explanation: Those are the native integrations named on the product overview. Scanning covers both cloud and on-premises assets.

questions.stem: What do Entro's machine learning models map?
choices: Relationships among services, users, and credentials, to show possible attack paths
Identity profile priority
Certification campaign deadlines
Password policy strength
questions.explanation: Individual findings are not the whole picture. The models connect services, users, and credentials so a path is visible.

questions.stem: How does Entro help a team act on what it finds?
choices: It integrates with ticketing and security orchestration platforms
It opens a Human Fabric certification automatically for every secret
It resets the secret's human owner password
It deletes the repository
questions.explanation: Mitigation is handed to the ticketing and orchestration tools the team already runs, after Entro has prioritized the secret.

questions.stem: What does scanning look for in source code and logs?
choices: Leaked credentials
Unsanctioned human lifecycles
Missing managers
Expired access requests
questions.explanation: Detection of leaked credentials in source code and logs is called out separately from the broader scan of cloud and on-premises assets.

questions.stem: What non-human population does Entro show inside development pipelines?
choices: Non-human identities used in those pipelines
Student accounts
Campaign owners
Identity Graph snapshots
questions.explanation: Pipeline visibility is one of the documented outcomes, next to continuous scanning and leaked-credential detection.

questions.stem: Why does the documentation mention deployment choice?
choices: So the customer can keep control of data locality and compliance
Because Entro runs only in one AWS region
Because scanning requires IdentityIQ
Because secrets cannot be classified in the cloud
questions.explanation: The overview ties deployment options to data locality and compliance. It does not describe Entro as a single fixed region.

questions.stem: What does real-time visibility cover besides repositories?
choices: Vaults and workloads
Only the current git commit
Human certification comments
Identity profile transforms
questions.explanation: The overview says centralized, real-time visibility across repositories, vaults, and workloads.

questions.stem: What makes two exposed secrets unequal in Entro?
choices: The risk level, which changes with privilege, rotation, and exposure
The order they were committed
Whether a human certified them
The connector category, Quick Compliance or Deep Governance
questions.explanation: Context-aware analysis exists so a team can prioritize. A privileged, unrotated, exposed secret is not treated the same as every other finding.

questions.stem: Which gap is Entro written to close?
choices: The gap between cloud providers, developer tools, and internal systems
The gap between joiner and leaver tickets
The gap between two identity profiles
The gap between a SIEM and a certification campaign
questions.explanation: That is the bridging sentence on the about page. Secrets leak in the spaces those systems do not share a view of.

questions.stem: What engine runs a Privileged Task Automation workflow?
choices: SailPoint's Workflows engine
A standalone script host
IdentityIQ's task scheduler only
The browser extension
questions.explanation: Privileged Task Automation is documented as workflow automation for privileged tasks, built on the Workflows engine inside Human Fabric.

questions.stem: What security outcome does automating the task produce?
choices: Standing privilege is removed, because the user no longer needs the credential to perform the action
The user is granted permanent Domain Admin
The credential is emailed to the technician
The vault is disabled
questions.explanation: The documented benefits are automating privileged processes, removing standing privilege, and reducing the need for specialized manual work.

questions.stem: How can a Privileged Task Automation workflow be created?
choices: From a template, in the visual builder, or by uploading JSON that includes a Privileged Task Automation action
Only by a support ticket
Only from an IdentityIQ rule
Only by editing an existing Harbor Pilot workflow
questions.explanation: Those are the three documented starting points. Uploaded JSON still has to include the Privileged Task Automation action.

questions.stem: When can a privileged task run with no one filling in a form?
choices: When it needs no user input. After it is enabled, the schedule or event runs it
Never. Every task requires the Launchpad
Only on the first day it is created
Only if Parameter Storage is empty
questions.explanation: Tasks with no inputs run behind the scenes. Tasks that need input must start with the Interactive Trigger, which creates the launcher.

questions.stem: What is created when a workflow uses an Interactive Trigger?
choices: A launcher, and an entitlement is created automatically so the task can be delegated
A new identity profile
A certification campaign
A Shared Signals transmitter
questions.explanation: The launcher is how a user starts the interactive process. Delegation is granting the entitlement that the launcher created. Until someone has that entitlement, they cannot run the task.

questions.stem: Where are privileged credentials referenced from during the action?
choices: Parameter Storage or a credential provider, and the action uses them without showing the values
The technician's browser
The certification sign-off comment
An email to the source owner
questions.explanation: Authentication details are secrets on the workflow. Parameter Storage is the SailPoint-managed repository. A credential provider is the other documented option. The Privilege Gateway virtual appliance uses them to reach the target.

questions.stem: What three kinds of parameters does Parameter Storage hold?
choices: Authentication, connection, and authorization
Joiner, mover, and leaver
Easy, medium, and hard
Subject, event, and stream
questions.explanation: Authentication is the username and secret. Connection is the host, address, or URL. Authorization is what the action is allowed to do. Admins update them in one place.

questions.stem: Who can see the secret value when a Privileged Action uses a stored parameter?
choices: The admin building the action cannot see the stored value
Every user on the Launchpad
The certification reviewer
Anyone with Workflows Read Only
questions.explanation: Parameter Storage is documented so the action can use authentication and connection parameters without exposing their values to the admin.

questions.stem: Where is Parameter Storage available?
choices: Only in AWS regions where the AWS Nitro Enclaves SailPoint uses are supported
In every region, including those without Nitro Enclaves
Only on premises
Only inside IdentityIQ
questions.explanation: The product page states that regional limit directly. It is a SailPoint-managed repository so customers do not have to bring their own secret store.

questions.stem: What does the Privilege Gateway virtual appliance do?
choices: It uses the stored credential to authenticate to the target and run the action
It stores identity profiles
It hosts the certification user interface
It replaces the browser extension
questions.explanation: The workflow's secrets authenticate the gateway onto the target application. The person who launched the task does not receive that credential.

questions.stem: What has to happen before the first privileged task can be automated?
choices: The site needs a way to supply privileged credentials, either Parameter Storage or a credential provider
Every human must be certified
Harbor Pilot must be enabled for end users
File Access Manager must be connected
questions.explanation: The setup section says to choose how privileged credentials will be provided before creating and automating tasks.

questions.stem: Can a privileged task be started by a person rather than by an event?
choices: Yes. The Interactive Trigger is the manual path, after the launcher is delegated
No. Tasks run only on a schedule
Only an Org Admin can type the command on the server
Only a SIEM alert can start one
questions.explanation: Workflows can start from a schedule or an event, or a user can start an interactive process. The interactive path is the one that requires delegation.

questions.stem: What is a privileged task, as the documentation defines it?
choices: Work that needs a privileged credential so someone can run commands on an application
Any access request
A role assigned by automation
A password reset email
questions.explanation: Privileged Task Automation elevates the work for the duration of the action and keeps the credential out of the user's hands.

questions.stem: What does Shadow AI Remediation show, and how does it respond?
choices: Real-time use of AI tools, with just-in-time remediation through guided playbooks
Only agents that were procured by central IT
SAP emergency access sessions
IdentityIQ login failures
questions.explanation: The product covers GenAI web applications and GenAI applications registered to the identity provider. Playbooks are the remediation path.

questions.stem: What are the two setup steps required before you can see usage?
choices: Connect an identity provider, then deploy the browser extension
Install a virtual appliance and a mainframe connector
Create an identity profile and a certification campaign
Enable Harbor Pilot for end users
questions.explanation: The identity provider supplies usage and risk. The browser extension discovers what users actually do in GenAI applications.

questions.stem: What does the browser extension fail to separate?
choices: Personal activity and business activity in any browser where it is installed
Sanctioned and unsanctioned applications
Entra and Okta
Admins and read-only users
questions.explanation: The documentation says the extension captures personal activity and that the customer is responsible for making that collection lawful. Privacy features can be turned off.

questions.stem: What do you define after the out-of-the-box GenAI application list?
choices: Which additional applications to log, and which applications policy allows
The SAP application servers
The identity profile priority
The form image limit
questions.explanation: You can add applications to the inventory, then mark the sanctioned set. Policy comes after that, and it has to be configured and tested.

questions.stem: Which identity providers are documented connection options?
choices: Microsoft Entra, Okta, and other identity providers
Only Active Directory on premises
Only SailPoint IdentityIQ
A CSV file and nothing else
questions.explanation: The admin guide has setup pages for Entra, Okta, and other IdPs. Connecting the IdP is what provides the inventory of registered GenAI applications.

questions.stem: Can privacy controls be changed after the extension is deployed?
choices: Yes. Privacy-related features can be managed and optionally disabled
No. The extension's collection settings are fixed
Only SailPoint Support can change them
Only by reinstalling IdentityIQ
questions.explanation: Configuring Privacy Controls is the documented place to change those features. The extension still does not itself distinguish personal and business activity.

questions.stem: What is a playbook in this product?
choices: Guided remediation for a GenAI policy decision, such as steering people away from a banned application
A Human Fabric certification template
A connector Express Setup
An IdentityIQ login configuration
questions.explanation: The overview points at playbooks for just-in-time remediation. Examples include avoiding banned GenAI apps and giving corporate GenAI policy guidance.

questions.stem: When do you decide the policy?
choices: After discovery is configured and sanctioned applications are defined, and then you test it
Before any identity provider is connected
Only after a certification is signed off
Policy is generated and cannot be tested
questions.explanation: The getting-started order is IdP, browser extension, review and extend the application list, define sanctioned apps, decide the policy, then configure and test it.

questions.stem: What does the identity provider connection provide that the extension does not replace?
choices: Visibility into AI usage and risk from applications registered to the IdP
Provisioning of human accounts
Password interception
SAP audit logs
questions.explanation: Both are required. The IdP shows registered GenAI applications. The extension discovers user activity in the browser.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for the personal data the extension collects?
choices: The customer, who must make sure collection and use comply with applicable requirements
SailPoint, because the extension is a SailPoint component
The end user, because they installed Chrome
The identity provider vendor
questions.explanation: The documentation states that responsibility directly next to the warning that personal and business activity are not distinguished.

questions.stem: What inventory do added applications feed?
choices: The inventory and dashboards that log the organization's GenAI activity
The Human Fabric identity profile list
The certification campaign archive
The Parameter Storage repository
questions.explanation: Adding an application is how activity that is not in the out-of-the-box list still shows up in those views.

questions.stem: What should be tested before you rely on a GenAI policy?
choices: The policy configuration itself, after sanctioned applications are defined
Only the virtual appliance heartbeat
IdentityIQ Access History partitions
The 90-day access-request timeout
questions.explanation: Configure and test is the last setup step in the overview. Discovery without a tested policy does not remediate.

questions.stem: Which two populations of GenAI applications does the product cover?
choices: GenAI web applications, and GenAI applications registered to the identity provider
Only sanctioned applications
Only applications built in IdentityIQ
Only desktop executables
questions.explanation: Those are the two scopes named at the top of the overview. Unsanctioned use is what the policy and playbooks then address.

questions.stem: How is Data Access Security delivered with Human Fabric?
choices: As an integrated SaaS solution that classifies data and remediates with workflows and governance policies
As an on-premises replacement for Human Fabric
As a File Access Manager upgrade
As a certification-only add-on with no discovery
questions.explanation: The product overview describes automated discovery and classification, built-in workflows, and out-of-the-box governance policies, integrated with Human Fabric.

questions.stem: Why would you create a virtual appliance for Data Access Security?
choices: To connect sources and load account data without opening the firewall
To store privileged task credentials
To host IdentityIQ
To disable data classification
questions.explanation: A virtual appliance is required when you want a direct connection that loads account data. It is the first mandatory setup item in the getting-started guide.

questions.stem: Who can grant Data Access Security user levels in Human Fabric?
choices: A Human Fabric admin. Users cannot grant user levels to themselves
Any Data Access Security user
The owner of a file share
The certification campaign reviewer
questions.explanation: User levels are Human Fabric permissions. The connect-to-Human-Fabric page says only a Human Fabric admin can grant or remove them, from Admin > Identities > Identity List.

questions.stem: Why connect Data Access Security to Human Fabric?
choices: To set permissions, add identities, and assign those identities to Data Access Security roles
To replace the virtual appliance
To scan git history
To provision SAP roles
questions.explanation: The connection is mandatory for permissions and identity assignment. Sources and an identity collector come after it.

questions.stem: Which sources should be created first?
choices: The few sources that together contain every user, because their data is the highest priority
The smallest file share
Sources that contain no accounts
Only cloud sources, after all on-premises sources
questions.explanation: Those priority sources are created first. Other sources can be added later. An identity collector is then created from a source so accounts and entitlements can be collected.

questions.stem: What does an identity collector do?
choices: Collects accounts and entitlements from a source you already created
Grants user levels
Writes file permissions back to the share with no review
Replaces the Human Fabric connection
questions.explanation: The collector is created from the source. Without it, Data Access Security does not have the accounts and entitlements from that source.

questions.stem: How does Data Access Security treat en-US and en-GB?
choices: Both behave as English. Territory distinctions are ignored, with Chinese called out as the exception
They are fully separate languages
Only en-US is supported
Locales are not configurable
questions.explanation: American English is the default, and more than 10 languages are supported. The docs say territory variants such as en-US and en-GB behave as en, and that Chinese is the exception.

questions.stem: What appears on the dashboard once aggregation is running?
choices: Tasks, approvals, and the rest of the operating views
Identity profile transforms
Harbor Pilot prompts
SAP security audit logs
questions.explanation: The getting-started guide points at the dashboard for tasks and approvals after data has been aggregated.

questions.stem: Where are the application-specific connection guides?
choices: The Data Access Security connector documentation
The IdentityIQ 8.3 install guide
The File Access Manager 8.3 portal
The password reset guide
questions.explanation: Data Access Security connects to many applications, and the getting-started page sends you to the DAS connector guides for each one.

questions.stem: What kind of risk is the product built to uncover?
choices: Hidden data risk, through discovery and classification of sensitive data
Only standing privileged accounts on the helpdesk
Only human joiner tickets
Only secrets in git history
questions.explanation: The overview centers on sensitive data and the security risk around it, with remediation through workflows and governance policies rather than a one-time scan.

questions.stem: Can a Data Access Security user assign themselves a Human Fabric user level?
choices: No. Only a Human Fabric admin can grant or remove user levels
Yes, from the Data Access Security dashboard
Yes, if they own a source
Only during the first aggregation
questions.explanation: That restriction is stated on the connect-to-Human-Fabric page. The admin path is Admin > Identities > Identity List.

questions.stem: What has to exist before an identity collector can be created?
choices: The source the collector will read
A completed certification campaign
Parameter Storage
An IdentityIQ task server
questions.explanation: The guide says to create the source first, then create the identity collector from it.

questions.stem: What is the default language?
choices: American English
British English as a distinct locale
The browser locale, including territory
Chinese
questions.explanation: American English is the default. Other languages are supported, but territory variants of a language are not treated as separate except for the documented Chinese exception.

questions.stem: What does Access Risk Management automate?
choices: Monitoring and managing access risk, including separation of duties and emergency access
Password resets for students
Browser-extension deployment
Machine account classification
questions.explanation: The overview names IT teams assessing SoD before access is granted, security teams governing emergency access, and audit and compliance teams using the reports.

questions.stem: When does an IT team use it relative to granting access?
choices: Before the access is granted, to assess separation-of-duties risk
Only after a yearly audit
After the user has had the access for 90 days
Only when a certification is unsigned
questions.explanation: The documented IT use is preventive: simulate and assess the SoD risk before the access exists, not only discover it later.

questions.stem: What do security teams govern with auditable controls?
choices: Emergency access workflows
Identity profile priority
Form placeholder text
Harbor Pilot prompts
questions.explanation: Emergency access is called out separately from ordinary access reviews. The control has to be auditable.

questions.stem: How many reports does the product documentation say it generates?
choices: Over 25, from high-level summaries to granular detail
One certification export
Three, one per cloud provider
None. Reports are an add-on
questions.explanation: Those reports are how audit teams lower the cost of evidence and how compliance teams speed the process. Simulation of role and user changes is the preventive companion.

questions.stem: How do you stop a risky role change from becoming production access?
choices: Simulate the role or user change before it is made
Wait for the next certification and revoke it then
Disable the ERP system
Shorten the Human Fabric request timeout
questions.explanation: The overview says to prevent risk by simulating role and user changes, managing access reviews, and governing emergency access requests.

questions.stem: What does Access Risk Management do with locale territory, such as a language variant?
choices: It does not recognize territory distinctions
It treats every territory as a separate language
It supports territory variants and nothing else
It requires en-US and rejects every other locale
questions.explanation: The getting-started note is that territory language distinctions are not recognized. Do not expect a regional variant to behave as its own language.

questions.stem: Why must every SAP application server be connected for emergency access monitoring?
choices: Security Audit Log activity is missed if any application server connection is left out
The extra servers improve report formatting only
SAP allows only one server, so the requirement is optional
Connections are needed for password sync, not for the audit log
questions.explanation: The emergency-access setup says you must add every application server connection or Security Audit Log will not track all EAM activity.

questions.stem: Which SAP log reader does the documentation recommend when RSAU_API_GET_LOG_DATA is not present but RSAU_READ_LOG is?
choices: RSAU_READ_LOG
SM20 on a 4.x system
The Human Fabric search index
A virtual appliance syslog
questions.explanation: RSAU_READ_LOG is the option when that function module exists but you are not on the release that provides RSAU_API_GET_LOG_DATA. Older ECC systems fall back to SM20 variants.

questions.stem: Who uses the reports to reduce audit cost?
choices: Audit teams, using automated audit-ready reports
End users resetting passwords
Developers scanning git history
Helpdesk staff unlocking accounts
questions.explanation: The overview assigns audit teams the cost outcome and compliance teams the speed outcome. Both depend on the same report set.

questions.stem: What else, besides simulation, keeps emergency access governable?
choices: Auditable controls on the emergency access workflow
Disabling the Security Audit Log
A single shared SAP account
Skipping application server connections
questions.explanation: Security teams are the audience for emergency access with auditable controls. The SAP configuration is what makes that activity visible.

questions.stem: Which ERP is the emergency-access setup page written for?
choices: SAP
Workday
ServiceNow
GitHub
questions.explanation: The setup page is the SAP emergency-access options, including how the Security Audit Log is read and how application servers are registered.

questions.stem: What happens if you monitor only some SAP application servers?
choices: Emergency access activity on the servers you skipped is not in the Security Audit Log collection
The other servers forward their logs automatically
Access Risk Management rejects the connection
Those servers are governed by Human Fabric certifications instead
questions.explanation: The requirement is explicit: add every application server connection so all EAM activity is tracked.

questions.stem: What kind of decision do the reports support?
choices: Data-informed decisions about access risk, at both summary and detail level
Which identity profile priority to set
Whether Harbor Pilot may edit a workflow
Which browser extension privacy toggle to use
questions.explanation: Over 25 reports is the mechanism. Simulation is how you test a change before it becomes one of those findings.

questions.stem: What populations does Non-Employee Risk Management manage?
choices: Non-employees such as contractors, vendors, and other partners
Employees in the HCM only
Machine accounts
SAP emergency-access ids
questions.explanation: The admin guide describes profiles for those populations and the data about them. End-user documentation is a separate User Help site.

questions.stem: Can Non-Employee Risk Management be the only copy of non-employee data?
choices: No. It can be an authoritative source, but the organization must keep a separate, regularly backed-up copy
Yes. SailPoint backs it up as the system of record
Yes, if workflows are enabled
Only when it is connected to Human Fabric
questions.explanation: The admin introduction says it should not be the sole repository. Backup guidance is in the Non-Employee API documentation, or through SailPoint Support.

questions.stem: What must the company obtain before putting personal data into the product?
choices: Consent from the data subjects, and a legal review of regulated data the contract restricts
A certification sign-off
An IdentityIQ license
A virtual appliance in every region
questions.explanation: The introduction restricts certain personal and regulated information and says to consult Legal. Consent is the company's responsibility before the data is included.

questions.stem: What determines which profiles a user can manage?
choices: The roles assigned when the user is added to the tenant
The identity profile priority in Human Fabric
Whether they own a source
The browser extension
questions.explanation: Roles gate profile management. Users you add help create, link, and manage non-employee data, but only within the profiles their roles allow.

questions.stem: What do you build before users can create profiles?
choices: Forms, assembled into pages, then profile types and a workflow set for each type
A certification campaign
Parameter Storage
An SAP application server connection
questions.explanation: Forms become the pages users fill in. Profile types categorize the data, such as the person, their organization, or a project. Each profile type needs its own create and update workflows.

questions.stem: Does one workflow set cover every profile type?
choices: No. Each profile type needs its own workflows
Yes. One create workflow serves every type
Workflows are optional if forms exist
Workflows are inherited from Human Fabric
questions.explanation: Users activate those workflows to create and update profiles of that type. A type without workflows cannot be managed the way the guide describes.

questions.stem: How do profiles become a map of the non-employee population?
choices: Profiles of different types are linked together
They are correlated by a machine account subtype
They are exported to a certification and not stored
They replace the HCM automatically
questions.explanation: Once profile types and workflows exist, you create profiles and link them until the organization has the non-employee map it needs.

questions.stem: What should you track to confirm the system is working?
choices: User activity and workflow activity
Harbor Pilot prompt quality
Identity Graph snapshots
SAP SM20 column layout
questions.explanation: The admin guide points at user reports and workflow-activity details for that check.

questions.stem: Where is the documentation for the people filling in profiles?
choices: The Non-Employee Risk Management User Help, separate from the admin guide
The IdentityIQ getting-started page
The connector landing page
Parameter Storage
questions.explanation: The admin page links User Help for end users of the non-employee system. Admin Help is the configuration guide.

questions.stem: What is an example of a profile type besides the non-employee themselves?
choices: The organization they come from, or the project they are working on
A Human Fabric identity profile
A machine account subtype
A Shared Signals stream
questions.explanation: Profile types categorize the data. The person, the vendor organization, and the project are the examples the admin guide gives.

questions.stem: Who should you ask before loading regulated personal information?
choices: Your legal department, because the contract and the product both restrict categories of data
The certification campaign owner
The source sub-admin
The browser-extension user
questions.explanation: The restriction is contractual as well as product-level. Consent from the data subject is a separate obligation the company has to meet.

questions.stem: How do users create a profile after configuration?
choices: They activate the create workflow for that profile type and complete its pages
They aggregate a source
They submit a Human Fabric access request
They edit the identity profile mapping
questions.explanation: Workflows are what users run to create and update profiles. The pages on those workflows are the forms you built.

questions.stem: What is the product allowed to be for identity governance?
choices: An authoritative source of non-employee information, with another backup kept elsewhere
The only repository, because SailPoint guarantees the backup
A read-only report that cannot store profiles
A replacement for the employee HCM
questions.explanation: Authoritative is allowed. Sole repository is not. The organization remains responsible for a separate, regularly backed-up source.

questions.stem: What does CIEM add to identity governance?
choices: Effective access on cloud entitlements, and what users do with that access
A replacement for Human Fabric certifications
Git secret scanning
Non-employee profile types
questions.explanation: CIEM is the deeper view of effective access to cloud resources and of entitlement activity. You manage those entitlements in Human Fabric after the cloud providers are connected.

questions.stem: What has to happen before cloud entitlements can be managed?
choices: Configure the cloud service providers and connect them to Human Fabric
Enable Harbor Pilot
Install IdentityIQ
Create a Non-Employee profile type
questions.explanation: The overview lists AWS, Azure, GCP, and Okta as the providers, each with its own configuration and Human Fabric connection.

questions.stem: Which cloud providers does the CIEM overview tell you to configure?
choices: AWS, Azure, GCP, and Okta
Only AWS
SAP and Workday
GitHub and Jenkins
questions.explanation: Each provider has a configuration page and a Human Fabric connection page. Entitlements are then managed inside Human Fabric.

questions.stem: Can you turn on CIEM inside the AWS SaaS connector and also use the CIEM connector for the same management account?
choices: No. Those two cannot both be enabled for the same management account
Yes. They are required together
Only in GovCloud
Only if Identity Center is disabled
questions.explanation: The AWS connection page states that conflict directly. The CIEM connector can still collect data for AWS SaaS accounts and entitlements when those entitlements are marked as cloud.

questions.stem: In what order do you connect the AWS source and the CIEM AWS source?
choices: Either order
The CIEM connector must be first
The SaaS connector must finish aggregating before CIEM can be created
Only after a certification is complete
questions.explanation: The connection page says the two sources may be connected in any order.

choices: Two
One SaaS connector covers both
None. CIEM reads them without a connector
One virtual appliance and no connector
questions.explanation: The page says both populations require two connectors. Identity Center users are managed with the CIEM AWS connector. IAM users use an AWS connector, with the SaaS connector recommended.

questions.stem: Which connector does the documentation recommend for IAM users?
choices: The SaaS-based AWS connector
A mainframe connector
The IdentityIQ connector
Express Setup for a read-only mainframe
questions.explanation: The implementation table lists the SaaS connector as recommended, with a VA-based connector as the alternative. A VA-based IAM connection also requires the CIEM AWS connector.

questions.stem: How do you govern Identity Center users when you are not governing IAM users?
choices: Connect the CIEM AWS connector. An IAM connector is not required for that option
Enable CIEM on the AWS SaaS connector for the same account
Use a Quick Compliance connector only
Mark nothing. Identity Center is out of scope
questions.explanation: The Identity Center-only path is the CIEM AWS connector. The both-populations path adds a separate IAM connector.

questions.stem: What do you do after cloud accounts and entitlements have aggregated?
choices: Mark the IAM entitlements, the Identity Center entitlements, or both, as cloud entitlements
Delete the AWS source
Disable effective-access calculation
Move the accounts to an identity profile
questions.explanation: Marking is what lets CIEM treat those entitlements as cloud access. The connection page says to mark IAM and/or Identity Center entitlements after aggregation.

questions.stem: A VA-based connection for IAM users without Identity Center still needs which other connector?
choices: The CIEM AWS connector
No other connector
A Deep Governance mainframe connector
The Non-Employee connector
questions.explanation: The table says a VA-based IAM connection requires the CIEM AWS connector as well. The SaaS-based IAM connector is the path that does not add that requirement for the IAM-only case.

questions.stem: Where do you manage the cloud entitlements once the providers are connected?
choices: In SailPoint Human Fabric
Only in the cloud provider console
In IdentityIQ Access History
In the browser extension
questions.explanation: CIEM's overview says configuration happens at the provider, and management of the entitlements happens in Human Fabric.

questions.stem: What will the CIEM connector still collect if you are not enabling CIEM on the AWS SaaS connector?
choices: Data for AWS SaaS accounts and entitlements, as long as they are marked as cloud
Nothing from the SaaS source
Human identity profiles
SAP audit logs
questions.explanation: That collection continues even though you cannot enable CIEM in the SaaS connector for a management account that already uses the CIEM connector.

questions.stem: What does effective access mean in this product?
choices: The cloud resources an entitlement can actually reach, plus activity on those entitlements
The role name stored in Human Fabric, ignoring the cloud policy
Whether the user has signed in to Human Fabric
The certification decision, regardless of the cloud grant
questions.explanation: The overview defines CIEM as the deeper view of effective access to resources and of users' entitlement activity in cloud infrastructure.

questions.stem: What does the Application Visibility documentation say it finds?
choices: Commercial SaaS, in-house applications, and unsanctioned shadow IT
Only applications already in Human Fabric
Only mainframe accounts
Only GenAI chatbots

questions.stem: What do you connect before the browser extension?
choices: The identity provider, so SaaS usage and risk are visible
A virtual appliance cluster
SAP application servers
Parameter Storage
questions.explanation: The identity provider connection comes first. The browser extension is what then discovers user activity.

questions.stem: What personal-data warning applies to the Application Visibility browser extension?
choices: It does not distinguish personal and business activity, and privacy features can be disabled
It captures business applications only
It never runs in a personal browser profile
Personal activity is filtered before it is stored
questions.explanation: The customer is responsible for lawful collection. Privacy controls are configurable. The same warning is documented for this extension.

choices: A user with the Org Admin user level
Any user who can see the inventory
A certification reviewer
A read-only administrator
questions.explanation: Org Admin is required to administer. Cert Admin, Helpdesk Admin, or Report Admin can have read-only access.

choices: Retrieve and view data, but not modify or delete it
Change privacy controls
Assign Org Admin
Delete discovered applications
questions.explanation: Global Administrator has full access, including system configuration and privacy controls. Read-only Administrator is limited to viewing.

questions.stem: What inventories exist after the identity provider and extension are in place?
choices: Applications, user accounts, and accounts discovered by the extension and the identity provider
Only a list of Human Fabric sources
Only sanctioned applications
Certification sign-off history
questions.explanation: Those inventories are the operating view. They include what the extension and the identity provider discovered, not only what was registered in advance.

questions.stem: Which Human Fabric user levels receive read-only access?
choices: Cert Admin, Helpdesk Admin, or Report Admin
Org Admin only
Identity Graph Read Only
Source Sub-Admin
questions.explanation: The overview names those three for read-only access to Application Visibility. Org Admin is the administrative level.

questions.stem: What does a Global Administrator configure that a read-only administrator cannot?
choices: System configuration and privacy controls
Nothing. The roles are identical
Only the inventory sort order
SAP emergency access
questions.explanation: Full access includes the admin console, product configuration, system configuration, and privacy controls.

questions.stem: How do you know which portal URL to use?
choices: From the URL in the initial connectivity instructions, which depends on the tenant region
Everyone uses the same URL
The URL is the Human Fabric admin console
The URL is documentation.sailpoint.com
questions.explanation: The guide branches on the domain in those instructions. One documented example is app.us-east4.savvy.security.

questions.stem: What kinds of applications count as shadow IT here?
choices: Unsanctioned applications running in the environment
Applications with a Deep Governance connector
Applications created as identity profiles
Applications that have completed a certification
questions.explanation: The overview groups commercial apps, in-house apps, and unsanctioned apps together as what Application Visibility is meant to see.

questions.stem: What discovers user-related activity after the identity provider is connected?
choices: The browser extension
A virtual appliance
Account aggregation
Access History
questions.explanation: The extension is the second setup step. Without it, the identity provider connection does not discover that user activity.

questions.stem: Can privacy-related features be turned off?
choices: Yes. They can be managed and optionally disabled
No. They are fixed for the life of the tenant
Only by uninstalling the identity provider
Only for read-only administrators
questions.explanation: Configuring Privacy Controls is the documented place. Global Administrators are the role that can define those controls.

questions.stem: What is a Global Administrator allowed to do in the admin console?
choices: Configure and manage the whole product, including system configuration and privacy controls
View inventories only
Read certifications and nothing else
Reset Human Fabric passwords
questions.explanation: That is the full-access role. Read-only Administrator cannot modify or delete.

questions.stem: What do the Identity Security connector guides cover?
choices: Connectivity for Human Fabric and Agentic Fabric
IdentityIQ 8.3 only
File Access Manager connectors
Non-Employee profile forms
questions.explanation: The landing page says the connectivity documentation covers Human Fabric and Agentic Fabric. IdentityIQ connectors are a separate landing page.

questions.stem: How do you find which tab a source belongs on?
choices: Search for the source name if you are not sure which category tab to open
Every source is on the Quick Compliance tab
Sources are listed only in IdentityIQ
The tab is chosen by the identity profile priority
questions.explanation: The landing page tells you to use the category tabs or the search field when you do not know where a source is listed.

questions.stem: What is a Quick Compliance connector for?
choices: User and entitlement aggregation with a lightweight, read-only setup so compliance work can start quickly
Provisioning account changes back to the source
Replacing a virtual appliance cluster
Storing privileged credentials
questions.explanation: Express Setup creates that read-only connection with minimal configuration. After it succeeds, you are prompted to run an aggregation.

questions.stem: What does Express Setup ask you to do after the connection succeeds?
choices: Run an aggregation
Enable write-back provisioning
Create a Privileged Task Automation workflow
Disable the source
questions.explanation: The prompt to aggregate is part of the Quick Compliance setup. The connection itself stays read-only.

questions.stem: What do Deep Governance connectors do that Quick Compliance connectors do not?
choices: They provision changes from Identity Security back to the managed system, as well as reading accounts
They are read-only and cannot aggregate entitlements
They work only with mainframes
They replace the need for an authoritative source
questions.explanation: Deep Governance reads user account data and provisions changes. Quick Compliance is the lightweight read-only path for compliance operations.

questions.stem: Which Deep Governance connectors require a virtual appliance cluster?
choices: VA-based connectors. SaaS-based connectors do not
All Deep Governance connectors
None. Deep Governance is always SaaS
Only the connectors marked for IdentityIQ
questions.explanation: The landing page draws that line explicitly. A VA-based connector needs the cluster. A SaaS-based connector does not.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for the API keys a connector needs?
choices: The customer. SailPoint is not responsible for the availability of those keys or permissions
SailPoint Support, as part of the connector
The source vendor ships them inside the connector
They are stored in Parameter Storage automatically
questions.explanation: The connectivity landing page says the customer maintains the API keys and other credentials required to reach the outside technology.

questions.stem: What does a successful Express Setup not do?
choices: Provision changes back to the target. The connection is read-only
Aggregate users
Aggregate entitlements
Prompt you to aggregate
questions.explanation: Quick Compliance is aggregation for compliance, with lightweight configuration. Provisioning is the Deep Governance distinction.

questions.stem: Where is Epic connector documentation kept?
choices: In the knowledge base, and you join the user group to view it
On the public Deep Governance tab, with no extra access
In the IdentityIQ 8.3 guide only
It is not documented
questions.explanation: The Deep Governance page says Epic and Epic SER documentation is in the knowledge base and requires the user group.

questions.stem: What is the practical difference you would tell a customer choosing a connector category?
choices: Quick Compliance gets to aggregation and compliance fast, and Deep Governance also writes changes back
They are the same connector with two names
Quick Compliance is for provisioning and Deep Governance is read-only
Deep Governance cannot aggregate entitlements
questions.explanation: That split is the landing page's reason for the two tabs. Express Setup is the fast read-only path. Deep Governance is the path that provisions.

questions.stem: A mainframe connector listed as read-only belongs to which story?
choices: Deep Governance still includes read-only mainframe connectors such as Top Secret and RACF
Read-only means it is a Quick Compliance connector
Read-only mainframe connectors provision changes
Mainframe connectors are unsupported
questions.explanation: The Deep Governance list includes Mainframe Top Secret and IBM RACF marked read-only. Read-only describes that connector's operations, not which tab it sits on.

questions.stem: What should the customer have ready before a connector can be used?
choices: The API keys and permissions the target technology requires
A completed role model
Harbor Pilot enabled for end users
An IdentityIQ MFA provider
questions.explanation: SailPoint does not supply those keys. The landing page assigns that responsibility to the customer.

questions.stem: After Express Setup, what data can the Quick Compliance connector bring in?
choices: Users and entitlements
Provisioning policies only
Privileged task credentials
Non-employee profile types
questions.explanation: User and entitlement aggregation is the stated scope, so compliance operations can start without a full write-back integration.

questions.stem: What does IdentityIQ warn you not to do while you are working?
choices: Open the same session in multiple tabs or browsers, because one can overwrite the other
Use MFA
Set a password policy
Enable Access History
questions.explanation: The getting-started guide says opening multiple tabs might overwrite changes made in another tab.

questions.stem: If your password is expired, when do you complete MFA?
choices: Before the password change. The MFA provider's page appears after the IdentityIQ login page
After the password has been changed
MFA is skipped when a password is expired
Only if you have a single provider
questions.explanation: You log in on the IdentityIQ page, then the MFA provider's page. An expired or required password change still goes through MFA first.

questions.stem: What do you do if you are assigned more than one MFA provider?
choices: Select a provider from the list before that provider's login page
IdentityIQ picks one automatically
Use all of them in sequence
MFA is disabled until an admin removes the extras
questions.explanation: The getting-started guide says the provider list is a required choice when more than one provider is assigned.

questions.stem: What has to be true before authentication questions can reset a password?
choices: An administrator has enabled the option, and you have already answered the questions in User Preferences
The questions work the first time you need a reset, with no prior setup
A mobile number is enough
Access History must be enabled
questions.explanation: The guide also distinguishes how many answers you must define from how many correct answers you must provide. If you never set them up, you contact the help desk or an IdentityIQ administrator.

questions.stem: What does a new password have to satisfy?
choices: The password policy the IdentityIQ administrator configured
A fixed eight-character rule that cannot be changed
The Human Fabric dictionary check
No policy. Any value is accepted
questions.explanation: The reset flow enforces the policy that was configured in IdentityIQ. It is not a universal rule documented as a fixed length.

questions.stem: What is required for a mobile reset option?
choices: An administrator enables it, and the account has a full mobile number including the area code
Any phone number, including one without an area code
The user enables it themselves with no administrator step
A Shared Signals transmitter
questions.explanation: The getting-started guide says the number must be complete, including the area code, and that an administrator activates the option.

questions.stem: How often does Access History run by default?
choices: Once per day, and the frequency can be configured
Every hour, and the schedule cannot be changed
Only when an administrator clicks a button
It is always on and has no task
questions.explanation: History events are published through a scheduled or ad hoc service. The default for the Access History run is daily.

questions.stem: Why is the first Dispatch Access History run slower than later runs?
choices: The first run extracts all identity and related objects. Later runs extract what is new or significantly changed
Later runs re-extract everything
The first run extracts only changed objects
Access History never extracts identities
questions.explanation: Unchanged objects are not processed again. The system also distinguishes initial events from change events and skips duplicates.

questions.stem: What happens if the host running a Dispatch Access History partition fails?
choices: Another host can resume from the last saved progress. The partition does not have to start over
The entire history database is rebuilt
That partition's objects are skipped permanently
Access History disables itself
questions.explanation: Each partition periodically saves progress inside its work cycle. That saved state is what another host resumes.

questions.stem: Is Access History available the moment IdentityIQ is installed?
choices: No. It is disabled by default until the history database and task are configured
Yes. It is enabled and runs hourly
Yes, but only for roles
It cannot be enabled
questions.explanation: The guide says Access History is disabled by default so you can configure it, including the database and tables and the task restrictions.

questions.stem: What does the Access History user interface search?
choices: The access history database, including identities, roles, entitlements, certifications, and requests
The live IdentityIQ tables only, with no separate history store
Human Fabric search
The SAP security audit log
questions.explanation: Extracted objects are stored in tables used by the Access History UI. APIs query that database for identities, roles, entitlements, certifications, requests, and managed attributes.

questions.stem: Who do you contact if authentication questions were never set up and you do not know your password?
choices: The help desk or an IdentityIQ administrator
SailPoint Harbor Pilot
The certification campaign owner
The cloud service provider
questions.explanation: The self-service question flow is unavailable until the answers exist in User Preferences. Until then, a person has to reset the password.

questions.stem: What can self-service registration do?
choices: Let a new user request an IdentityIQ account the first time they open the product, if an administrator enabled it
Create an account with no administrator action, always
Reset a password without MFA
Enable Access History
questions.explanation: Registration can also be opened from a direct link that skips the login page. The option has to be enabled, and the user completes the required fields, including the requested identity.
